distance.label: Estimated road miles = great-circle miles × 1.14
distance.source: OSRM driving route divided by the great-circle distance, mean of six routes
distance.measured: Queried the public OSRM driving router on 2026-10-25. Ratios of driving miles to great-circle miles: Rockville ZIP 20850 to Parrish 1.117 (949.4 / 850.0), New York ZIP 10001 to Sarasota 1.134 (1187.4 / 1046.6), Chicago ZIP 60601 to Lakewood Ranch 1.138 (1185.6 / 1042.0), Atlanta ZIP 30303 to Venice 1.096 (518.7 / 473.3), Boston ZIP 02108 to Tampa 1.137 (1344.7 / 1182.2), Columbus ZIP 43215 to North Port 1.221 (1090.1 / 893.1). Mean 1.1405, used as 1.14.
distance.caveat: Not a routed distance for every ZIP. The 1.14 factor is the mean of those six measured ratios. Alaska uses the same factor; a separate Alaska Highway route was not returned by the router in this check.

movers.label: Full-service long-distance mover, typical low, median, and typical high booked price
movers.source: ConsumerMovingReviews (CMR) Moving Cost Report 2026, price bands CSV (booked estimates, not invoices)
movers.caveat: Cells marked limited sample are widened in the estimator (low × 0.75, high × 1.25) and then held so a longer move is not cheaper. The 1,500-1,999 miles / 4+ bedroom cell still covers Dec 2022-Sep 2026; the CMR CSV was not republished with a newer figure for that cell when checked 2026-10-25. Where a published longer-distance cell was below the previous band, the stored cell is held at the previous band. The published figures are in movers.published.

published.note: Published CMR cells before the longer-move hold. A longer band that was below the previous band is held at the previous figure in low, median, and high so a longer move is not cheaper.

hah.label: HireAHelper average move cost tables (local <50 mi; long-distance 1,200 mi)
hah.source: HireAHelper Moving Cost Calculator, 2026 tables (Transportation Cost Database + transaction data)
hah.caveat: The local table is published for moves under 50 miles and is the price under 50 miles. The 1,200-mile full-service table supplies the house-to-apartment ratio. DIY truck and container prices start at the local table and rise through the Maryland-to-Florida guide at 949 miles, then keep that per-mile slope. They are not held at the 1,200-mile HireAHelper figure, and they stay at or under full-service for the same home.

initReg.label: FL initial registration fee (per vehicle new to FL)

regTax.label: FL base vehicle tax by weight
regTax.caveat: Autos 2,499 lb or less $14.50; 2,500-3,499 lb $22.50; 3,500 lb or more $32.50. Base vehicle tax only. Other statutory fees apply.

dl.label: FL original Class E driver license
dl.caveat: An additional $6.25 service fee may apply at a tax collector office.

gas.label: FL avg regular gasoline $/gal
gas.measured: AAA state gas-price averages page read 2026-10-25. Florida regular $4.1084. The earlier $4.057 figure was the Oct 22, 2026 AAA Florida price.
gas.caveat: Regular gasoline. A drive uses the lower of the origin-state and Florida AAA prices as low, the higher as high, and the average as typical. Same-state drives use the one published average for all three.

lodging.label: Standard CONUS lodging per diem
lodging.caveat: Federal lodging cap, used as a lodging proxy. Not a hotel quote.

packing.label: Packing service (partial or full)
packing.source: Element Moving, Dallas packing table by home size; AmeriSafe partial range; moveBuddha Maryland-to-Florida add-ons

ship.label: Vehicle shipping (auto transport)
ship.source: RoadRunner Auto Transport, Maryland to Florida car shipping, city-pair table and corridor average

storage.label: Storage unit
storage.source: moveBuddha, Maryland to Florida, storage-in-transit per month

airfare.label: Airfare to Florida
airfare.source: Planning range for a one-way Washington-area to Tampa or Sarasota ticket. Not confirmed on a BTS or airline fare table.

meals.label: Standard CONUS meals and incidental expenses
meals.caveat: Standard M&IE is $68. Published tiers run higher in some places; this estimator uses the standard rate. A drive that fits in one day does not add M&IE. When the trip includes a night, the first and last travel day are counted at 75%.

diyScale.label: DIY truck and container distance scaling
diyScale.source: Scaled from the HireAHelper local and 1,200-mile tables. Not a second published table.
diyScale.caveat: Typical price moves in a straight line from the HireAHelper local price at 0 miles through the Maryland-to-Florida guide at 949 miles, then keeps that per-mile slope. It is kept at or under full-service. Low is 0.8 times the local typical and high is 1.25 times it. Those two ends are an assumption.

fullLocal.label: Local full-service range
fullLocal.source: HireAHelper local table, with a low and high added by this estimator
fullLocal.caveat: The published local figure is the typical price. Low is 0.75 times that figure and high is 1.25 times that figure.

fullBridge.label: 50 to 300 mile full-service blend
fullBridge.source: Blended from the HireAHelper local table at 50 miles to the CMR band midpoint at 300 miles
fullBridge.caveat: From 50 to 300 miles the price moves in a straight line from the local table at 50 miles to the long-distance band at 300 miles. The under-50-mile table is not used as the price for that span.

carMpg.label: Car fuel economy
carMpg.source: Assumption for a cost range. Not an EPA figure.
carMpg.caveat: High cost uses 20 mpg, typical 25, and low cost 30. Gasoline uses the lower, the average, and the higher of the origin-state AAA price and the Florida price. A same-state drive uses the one published average.

truckMpg.label: Rental truck fuel economy
truckMpg.source: GoodMigrations uses 10 miles per gallon for the Maryland-to-Florida truck example. This estimator uses that figure for low, typical, and high.
truckMpg.measured: GoodMigrations FAQ: at 10 miles per gallon, the 949-mile drive burns about 94 gallons.

milesPerDay.label: Miles driven per day
milesPerDay.source: Assumption used only to count nights and meal days.
milesPerDay.caveat: Nights are zero or more, from ceil(miles divided by miles per day) minus 1. Fewer miles per day means more nights and a higher cost. Meal days are zero when that pace fits the drive into one day.

rooms.label: Hotel rooms
rooms.source: Two adults per room on every column.
rooms.caveat: Rooms are one for every two adults, rounded up, on low, typical, and high. The range comes from nights and, when the adult count is not chosen, from that spread.

adultsUnsure.label: Adults when not chosen
adultsUnsure.source: Assumption used only when the adult count is Not sure.

limitedSample.label: Wider range for CMR cells marked limited sample
limitedSample.source: The CMR cells are marked limited sample by CMR. The width is this estimator's allowance, not a second published price.
limitedSample.caveat: Low is 0.75 times the cell and high is 1.25 times the cell. The result is then held so a longer move is not cheaper than a shorter one.

routeGuide.measured: Opened the Freightwaves Checkpoint Maryland-to-Florida mover page (dated Oct 6, 2026) and the GoodMigrations Maryland-to-Florida page (updated October 2026) on 2026-10-25 and read the published tables.

full.source: Freightwaves Checkpoint, Maryland to Florida movers, home-size table

full2brHigh.source: GoodMigrations, Maryland to Florida, 2-bedroom full-service range $2,221 to $5,111 on a 949-mile route
full2brHigh.measured: Read the FAQ answer "How Much Do Full-Service Movers Cost for a 2 Bedroom Home?" on the GoodMigrations page.

container.source: Freightwaves Checkpoint, Maryland to Florida, moving container table

truck.source: Freightwaves Checkpoint, Maryland to Florida, rental truck table

typical2br.source: GoodMigrations, rental truck average for a 2 to 3 bedroom load, Maryland to Florida
typical2br.measured: FAQ: "A rental truck is the cheapest way to move from Maryland to Florida, averaging $700 for a 2 to 3 bedroom load."

sizeHold.source: Freightwaves Checkpoint rental-truck table and GoodMigrations truck typical, Maryland to Florida
sizeHold.caveat: The published 2-bedroom truck price is not above the 1-bedroom, so those sizes are held equal. No extra dollar is added.
sizeHold.measured: Freightwaves 2-bedroom rental truck is $648–$1,217. The 1-bedroom range is $662–$1,218. The 2-bedroom low and high are not above the 1-bedroom. GoodMigrations says a rental truck averages $700 for a 2 to 3 bedroom load, which is below the 1-bedroom midpoint of $940. No published gap keeps a 2-bedroom truck inside the Freightwaves 2-bedroom high of $1,217 while staying strictly above the 1-bedroom. HireAHelper local and long-distance truck ratios are not applied, because they would put the 2-bedroom above that Freightwaves high. The estimator holds the 2-bedroom equal to the 1-bedroom.

ship.source: RoadRunner Auto Transport, Maryland to Florida car shipping, city-pair table and corridor average
ship.measured: Read the October 2026 RoadRunner page: corridor average $737, open range $450–$1,200, city-pair open rates listed above, SUVs and trucks add $100–$200, enclosed estimated at about 1.5× open. Freightwaves Checkpoint car-shipping page dated October 18, 2026, read the same day: $855–$1,223 for 949 miles (the September 9, 2026 page had $835–$1,375; that range was not on the page when reopened).
ship.caveat: Open-carrier sedan. At 500 miles and under, RoadRunner's under-500 open band is used ($300–$500; typical $400 is the midpoint of that band). From 500 miles the price rises in a straight line to the 751-mile Baltimore–Jacksonville price. From 751 to 1,097 miles, high follows the city pairs and does not fall. Low is a pool-adjacent-violators fit of the seven published lows, equal weight on each pair: $475 through 874 miles, then $545 from 901 through 1,097 miles. Past 1,097 miles the price moves to the 2,000+ open band and the $1,215 national average, then holds. Freightwaves $855–$1,223 is applied only inside the city-pair span. The published 28% October–November southbound spike is quoted and not applied. The $150 SUV typical is the midpoint of the published $100–$200 adder.

longHaul.source: RoadRunner car shipping calculator, 2026 national average and open-transport distance bands
longHaul.measured: Calculator page read 2026-10-25, updated October 2026: nationwide average $1,215 across thousands of shipments, median distance 987 miles, median $1.23 per mile. Open-transport bands: under 500 miles $300–$500, 500–1,000 $500–$800, 1,000–1,500 $700–$1,000, 1,500–2,000 $900–$1,200, 2,000+ miles $1,100–$1,600. The 2,000+ band is one published bucket, so the estimator moves from the last Maryland–Florida pair to that band by 2,000 miles and then holds. Typical uses the $1,215 national average, which sits inside the 2,000+ band. A separate cross-country typical was not published.
longHaul.caveat: Used only past the longest Maryland-to-Florida city pair. The $1,215 figure is the national average at a 987-mile median, not a quote for a 2,000-mile trip.

shortHaul.source: RoadRunner car shipping calculator, open-transport distance table, under 500 miles
shortHaul.measured: Distance table on the calculator page, Updated October 2026, read 2026-10-25: Under 500 miles, open transport $300–$500. Typical $400 is the midpoint of those published ends, not a separate published typical. A summary bullet also says a shipment under 500 miles typically costs $200–$500, and a 250-mile sample is $200. Those lower figures are not the distance-table band and are not used. The band holds through 500 miles, then the estimate rises in a straight line to the 751-mile Baltimore–Jacksonville price.

lowFit.weight: equal weight per published city pair
lowFit.pooled: The last five published lows, 650, 500, 550, 500, and 525, average (650+500+550+500+525)/5 = 545. The first two pairs stay at 475. Between 874 and 901 miles the low rises in a straight line from 475 to 545.
lowFit.source: RoadRunner Auto Transport, Maryland to Florida city-pair open rates, smoothed with pool-adjacent-violators
lowFit.measured: Seven published open lows, read 2026-10-25: Baltimore–Jacksonville 475, Gaithersburg–Orlando 475, Annapolis–Tallahassee 650, Rockville–Tampa 500, Hagerstown–St. Petersburg 550, Bowie–Hialeah 500, Frederick–Miami 525. Pool-adjacent-violators with equal weight on each pair merges the last five, because each one is below the running block average, into 545. The result does not fall as miles rise.

snowbird.quote: Prices on southbound Florida routes typically spike 28% in October and November.
snowbird.source: RoadRunner car shipping calculator, snowbird corridor
snowbird.measured: Calculator page, Updated October 2026, read 2026-10-25. The snowbird section says "Snowbird corridor: 28% price spike Oct–Nov" and "Prices on southbound Florida routes typically spike 28% in October and November." A separate bullet says rates rise through the fall snowbird season, September through December, and that bullet has no percent. January through March "saves … 20 to 25% versus peak snowbird season." The 28% is quoted on October and November moves that start outside Florida. It is not multiplied into the price.

packing.source: Element Moving, Dallas packing table by home size; AmeriSafe partial range; moveBuddha Maryland-to-Florida add-ons
packing.measured: Element table read 2026-10-25: studio/1-bedroom partial $150–$400, full $350–$800, materials $80–$220; 2-bedroom partial $250–$700, full $700–$1,400, materials $150–$350; 3-bedroom partial $500–$1,200, full $1,300–$2,600, materials $250–$550; 4+ partial $900–$2,000, full $2,400–$5,500, materials $400–$900. AmeriSafe partial packing $200–$500 (not split by size). moveBuddha Maryland-to-Florida full packing $520–$1,350 and materials $150–$430. The 2-bedroom row uses the lowest and highest of those published ends. Studio and 1-bedroom stay on Element's combined row. Typical is the midpoint of the published ends.
packing.caveat: Element's figures are a Dallas local-market table used for the home-size scale. The 2-bedroom ends also include AmeriSafe and the moveBuddha Maryland-to-Florida add-on. A 50% materials discount for partial packing is not published, so partial and full both use the materials range.

storage.source: moveBuddha, Maryland to Florida, storage-in-transit per month
storage.measured: Add-on table: Storage-in-transit (per month) $180–$430. Typical is the midpoint.
storage.caveat: Price is the monthly rate times the number of months. One month is used only when storage is selected and no month count was given.

airfare.source: US DOT Consumer Airfare Report, Table 1a, 2026 Q1 each-way fares, Washington-area airports to Tampa and Sarasota
airfare.measured: Dataset tfrh-tu9e, rows updated September 3, 2026, queried 2026-10-25 for year 2026 quarter 1. DOT says these averages are each-way prices, including taxes and airport fees, excluding free tickets and bag or seat fees. Airport pairs and passengers per day: DCA–TPA 1,020.26 fare $254.79 lowest-carrier $225.84; BWI–TPA 959.69 fare $243.74 lowest-carrier $139.45; IAD–TPA 634.72 fare $252.27 lowest-carrier $143.83; BWI–SRQ 354.19 fare $310.06 lowest-carrier $208.71; DCA–SRQ 221.12 fare $279.91 lowest-carrier $208.01; IAD–SRQ 83.49 fare $148.28 lowest-carrier $114.80. Passenger-weighted average of those six fares is $256.02. Low is the BWI–Tampa lowest-carrier average, $139.45, not rounded up to $140. High is the BWI–Sarasota average, $310.06. The thinner IAD–Sarasota lowest-carrier fare of $114.80 is not used as the low. The six-pair blend is used only when the nearest of these Table 1a airports is DCA, IAD, or BWI. Other origins use the nearest airport's own 2026 Q1 Tampa and Sarasota rows. 73 origin airports have at least one such row with 10 or more passengers a day (90 markets). Three thinner rows were left out: SWF–TPA 0.11 passengers/day; FNT–TPA 6.11 passengers/day; PHF–TPA 6.39 passengers/day.
airfare.caveat: Quarterly each-way average, not a quoted fare. The Washington-area blend is used only when the nearest Table 1a airport is DCA, IAD, or BWI. Any other origin uses that airport's own Tampa and Sarasota fares when a 2026 Q1 row has at least 10 passengers a day. If the nearest airport has no such row, the line is marked Estimate and uses the nearest airport that does. If the airport used is more than 150 miles from the start, the line is marked Estimate. The 150-mile line is this estimator's labeling rule, not a DOT rule. Origins in Florida are not given an airfare. On a flying trip the adult count is the number of new Florida licenses when that count is at least 1, otherwise 1, unless adults were chosen. The same count is used on low, typical, and high.

airportsSource.source: OurAirports airports.csv, coordinates for airports that appear in DOT Table 1a for 2026 Q1
airportsSource.measured: Retrieved 2026-10-25 from https://davidmegginson.github.io/ourairports-data/airports.csv (OurAirports, David Megginson). The airport list is the 147 codes that appear as airport_1 or airport_2 in Table 1a for year 2026 quarter 1, queried the same day. Coordinates are latitude_deg and longitude_deg, rounded to 4 decimal degrees. OurAirports labels the Palm Beach field as DJT (ident KPBI); DOT still uses PBI, and the PBI coordinates are that row. Fares are not taken from OurAirports.

stairs.source: moveBuddha stair or elevator carry $80–$260; Coastal Moving Services elevator $100–$400
stairs.measured: moveBuddha add-on table and Coastal hidden-cost table, read 2026-10-25. Low is moveBuddha's $80. High is Coastal's elevator high of $400. Typical is the midpoint of moveBuddha's $80–$260, which is $170.

longCarry.source: Coastal Moving Services, long carry $75 to $300+
longCarry.measured: Coastal table: Long Carry Fee $75 to $300+. Typical is the midpoint, $187.50. The source says $300 or more.

shuttle.source: moveBuddha, Maryland to Florida, shuttle service $200–$590
shuttle.measured: moveBuddha add-on table. Coastal publishes $200–$600. This line uses the moveBuddha route range. Typical is the midpoint, $395.
shuttle.caveat: Coastal Moving Services also publishes a shuttle of $200–$600.

valuation.source: Coastal Moving Services valuation upgrade $100–$500+; moveBuddha full-value protection 1%–2% of declared value; released value 60¢ per pound
valuation.measured: Coastal table: Valuation Upgrade $100 to $500+. moveBuddha add-on: Full-value protection 1%–2% of declared shipment value. No declared-value table by home size was published, so the dollar line uses Coastal's range and the note states the 1%–2% rule. Typical is the midpoint, $300. Released value at 60¢ per pound is included at no charge.
valuation.caveat: Optional. Basic released-value protection at 60¢ per pound is included at no charge. Coastal says the upgrade can be $500 or more. A $300–$800 2-bedroom inference was not used because no declared value was published.

lodgingTax.source: Florida DOR DR-15TDT (rev. 10/26) local transient tax; Sarasota and Manatee tax collectors for the combined rate
lodgingTax.measured: DR-15TDT lists a 6% local transient rental tax in Hillsborough, Pinellas, Manatee, and Sarasota, in addition to the 6% state sales tax. Sarasota Tax Collector: 6% tourist tax plus 7% state sales tax in Sarasota County. Manatee Tax Collector: total 13% (6% tourist development tax + 7% sales and use tax). Hillsborough and Pinellas use 12% (6% state + 6% local) because a discretionary surtax was not confirmed for those two counties.
lodgingTax.caveat: Applied on top of the GSA lodging cap. Hillsborough and Pinellas do not include an unconfirmed county surtax.

tow.source: U-Haul, tow dolly local daily rate
tow.measured: U-Haul towing-equipment table, page updated February 18, 2026: Tow Dolly daily local price $49.95. One-way national prices are not published. The estimator multiplies this daily rate by the travel days already used for lodging.
tow.caveat: Local daily rate times travel days. A one-way quote can differ. Taxes are not included. Used when one adult would otherwise have to drive the rental truck and a car.
